- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or too high after recent spikes; model overshoots and fails to correct downward quickly.
- Mean reversion is underappreciated — model holds high forecasts longer than actual price tends to revert to lower levels.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops; often fails to reduce forecast when true price starts declining.
- Forecasts show persistent upward bias in the middle-to-late period of 30d window, while true prices often dip or stabilize lower.
- Model overreacts to short-term volatility; forecasts amplify minor price swings rather than smoothing them.
- In cases with strong downward momentum, model fails to anticipate the full extent of the drop, leading to overestimation of future prices.
- Model tends to underestimate the magnitude of price corrections after spikes, especially in the 10–20 day window.
